objective: List every point of Moonshot's official guidance for prompting Kimi K3.1 Pro and the kimi-for-coding model (K2.8 Preview), with the source section of each, so a kimi-k3.1/guide.md can carry each point.
scope: Sources, in this order: https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/prompt-best-practice ; https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart ; https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-kimi-k3-to-setup-agent ; Moonshot's K3 tool-calling best-practice guide (find it under platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide). Fetch with the web tools you have (for example the Exa fetch tool). Background on what HolyAgent decided is in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0/docs/pi/providers.md.

For each page: every recommendation as one line in Moonshot's meaning (paraphrase, short quotes where wording matters), its section heading and URL with anchor where one exists; mark which points are request parameters (reasoning_effort, temperature, passing reasoning_content back, tool_choice) versus prompt-writing guidance. Note anything K2.8 Preview does differently if a page says so.
constraints: Sourced facts only; label any inference. The list is the deliverable, so the report may run to 2000 words; keep notes outside the list under 150 words.

result:
result: Four pages cover 39 points; none mention K2.8 Preview or kimi-for-coding. The tool-calling guide was read from search highlights, not a full fetch, and appeared complete to its closing "complete flow" list.

Tags: [PARAM] is a request parameter or API-contract rule, [PROMPT] is prompt-writing guidance, [LOOP] is agent-loop or tool-design guidance. Where a page gave no anchors, I name the section heading.

**Page 1. https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/prompt-best-practice** ("Best Practices for Prompts"; the fetch returned no anchors)

Section "Write Clear Instructions":
1. [PROMPT] Make instructions explicit, because "the model can't read your mind". Ask for brevity if output is too long, expert-level writing if too simple, and show the format you want. The less the model guesses, the better the result.
2. [PROMPT] Include all important details and context in the request. Section "Including More Details in Your Request Can Yield More Relevant Responses". The page contrasts a vague request with a specific one.
3. [PROMPT] Assign a role in the `messages` system message. Section "Requesting the Model to Assume a Role Can Yield More Accurate Output".
4. [PROMPT] Use delimiters (triple quotes, XML tags, section headings) to separate parts of the input that need different handling. Section "Using Delimiters in Your Request to Clearly Distinguish Different Parts of the Input".
5. [PROMPT] Spell out the steps of a task explicitly, because explicit steps are easier to follow and give better output. Section "Clearly Define the Steps Needed to Complete the Task".
6. [PROMPT] Give examples of the desired output (few-shot). General guidance with examples is "usually more efficient than showing all permutations of the task", and few-shot suits styles that are hard to describe. Section "Provide Examples of Desired Output to the Model".
7. [PROMPT] Specify output length, in words, sentences, paragraphs or bullets. Word counts are "not highly precise", and the model is better at a set number of paragraphs or bullets. Section "Specify the Desired Length of the Model's Output".

Section "Provide Reference Text":
8. [PROMPT] Supply credible reference text and tell the model to answer from it. Give a fallback such as "I can't find the answer" when the answer is absent. Section "Guide the Model to Use Reference Text to Answer Questions".

Section "Break Down Complex Tasks":
9. [PROMPT] For tasks with many independent instruction sets, classify the query type first. Then give only the instructions relevant to that class. Section "Categorize to Identify Instructions Relevant to User Queries".
10. [LOOP] In long dialogs, summarize or filter earlier turns because context is fixed. Summarize past rounds once a size threshold is hit, and carry the summary in the system message, or summarize asynchronously. Section "For Long-Running Dialog Applications, Summarize or Filter Previous Conversations".
11. [LOOP] For long documents, summarize chunk by chunk and then recursively summarize the summaries. Include summaries of earlier chapters when a later part depends on them. Section "Chunk and Recursively Build a Complete Summary for Long Documents".

**Page 2. https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart** ("Kimi K3.1 Pro"; no anchors in the fetch)

Section "Reasoning effort" and "Important limits":
12. [PARAM] Thinking is always on and cannot be disabled. Section "FAQ" ("How do I turn off Kimi K3.1 Pro's chain-of-thought?").
13. [PARAM] Set the top-level `reasoning_effort` to `low`, `high` or `max`, default `max`. Use `low` if reasoning takes too long. Sections "Reasoning effort", "Important limits" and "FAQ".
14. [PARAM] Return the complete assistant message unchanged on later turns, including `reasoning_content`, and not only `content`. Sections "Reasoning effort" and "Important limits".
15. [PARAM] `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `n=1`, `presence_penalty=0` and `frequency_penalty=0` are fixed, so omit them. Section "Important limits".
16. [PARAM] `max_completion_tokens` defaults to 131072 and can be raised to 1048576. Section "Important limits".

Section "Streaming":
17. [PARAM] Streaming yields separate `reasoning_content` and `content` deltas.

Section "Structured output":
18. [PARAM] Use `response_format` with `json_schema` and `strict: true`. Parse only `message.content`, never `reasoning_content`.

Sections "Vision input" and "Partial Mode":
19. [PARAM] Vision `content` must be an array of objects, not a serialized string. Public image URLs are unsupported, so use base64 or `ms://`.
20. [PARAM] Partial mode adds a final assistant message with `partial=True`. Prepend the prefix yourself when displaying the result.

Section "Custom tools and `tool_choice`":
21. [PARAM] Use `tool_choice="required"` on the first turn to force at least one tool call. After executing the calls, return the complete assistant message plus one tool result per call with the matching `tool_call_id`.

Section "Dynamic tool loading":
22. [PARAM] A `system` message carrying `tools` and no `content` makes the tool available from its position onward. Include the full `name`, `description` and `parameters`, and keep the message in later history because the server does not retain it.

Section "1M context and TTL caching":
23. [PARAM] Caching is automatic. TTL is `5m` by default, or `1h` via `prompt_cache_options.ttl` when gaps exceed 5 minutes. Partial cache blocks bill as misses.

Section "Official tools":
24. [LOOP] Official tools go through Formula: fetch `/tools`, add the definitions to `tools`, execute calls via `/fibers`, then return the tool message. Web search is "not recommended" in the near term.

**Page 3. https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-kimi-k3-to-setup-agent** ("Build an Agent with Kimi K3"; no anchors in the fetch)

Section "Break Down the Task":
25. [LOOP] Split work into retrieve, analyze and deliver before choosing tools or writing prompts. Let the model plan and judge while tools handle retrieval and deterministic work. Avoid repeating tool behavior in a long system prompt.

Section "Design Tools":
26. [LOOP] Use JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` and listed `required` fields to reduce invalid arguments.
27. [LOOP] For dozens or hundreds of tools, do not send every schema each request. Retrieve candidates first and load them dynamically.

Section "Design the Prompt":
28. [PROMPT] Keep the system prompt on role, workflow and quality boundaries, and leave argument details in the tool schema. The example prompt does the following:
   - Separate facts, estimates and inferences.
   - Support key findings with multiple sources.
   - Never fabricate data or sources, and state gaps when evidence is insufficient.
   - Name the required report sections.
   - Answer in the user's language.
29. [PROMPT] Add constraints incrementally as format, compliance or audience change.

Section "Configure the K3 API":
30. [PARAM] Always append the complete SDK assistant message to `messages`. Copying only `content` and `tool_calls` drops `reasoning_content` and "breaks the context needed by later tool calls". This is repeated as mandatory under "Complete Agent Loop".

Section "Complete Agent Loop":
31. [LOOP] Every tool message must carry the matching `tool_call_id`.
32. [LOOP] Cap tool rounds. The example uses `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 8` in a loop, not recursion.
33. [LOOP] Fail on `finish_reason="length"` instead of treating truncated output as final.
34. [LOOP] When one tool call fails, return its error as that call's tool result and continue the other calls in the round.

Section "Run and Troubleshoot":
35. [LOOP] If the round cap is hit, check for overlapping tool descriptions and ambiguous results, then narrow the task.
36. [LOOP] For repeated argument errors, fix the schema (`required`, `enum`, `additionalProperties`). "Do not replace argument constraints with prompt text".

Section "Custom Tools and Optimization":
37. [LOOP] Expose only the tools the current task needs, and avoid overlapping tools.
38. [LOOP] Validate tool inputs in the application and return structured errors so the model can correct its arguments.
39. [PARAM] Check the tool-calling guide and the Model Parameter Reference before using `tool_choice` or reasoning effort.

**Page 4. https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-tool-calling-best-practice** ("Kimi K3 API Tool Calling Best Practices")

Section "Declare a search tool, not all your tools":
40. [LOOP] With a large inventory, declare only a backend-implemented `search_tools` plus a few core tools. Large inventories "eat up context" and make wrong-tool picks more likely.
41. [PROMPT] Advertise the searchable domain tags in the system prompt so the model calls `search_tools` first.

Section "Use tool_choice to force first-turn retrieval":
42. [PARAM] Set `tool_choice: "required"` on the first turn so the model does not answer from memory. Switch back to `"auto"` afterward. Changing `tool_choice` does not invalidate the prefix cache.

Section "Inject tool definitions on demand":
43. [PARAM] Insert the matched tools' full declarations through a `system` message with a `tools` field. They are visible from that position, use the same format as top-level `tools`, and coexist with them.
44. [PARAM] Declarations are per request and not retained by the server. Keep the original declaration in later requests to keep the tool callable and the prefix cache reusable. If it is dropped, the model cannot call the tool and the cache may miss.

Section "Pick the reasoning effort for the task":
45. [PARAM] `reasoning_effort` is `low`, `high` or `max` (default `max`). Decide it before the conversation starts. Appending a tool declaration at the end of `messages` does not affect the cached prefix. Removing or changing an earlier declaration may break cache hits after that point.

Section "The complete flow" is a five-step recap of items 40 and 42 to 45.

**Closely related pages** (not among the four, but cited by them and returned by search)
- https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-tool-choice
  - `"required"` forces at least one call.
  - `"none"` gives text only and saves latency and tokens.
  - `"auto"` is the default.
  - A function object forces a specific tool, but it returns 400 with thinking enabled. K3.1 Pro always thinks, so this form is unusable on it.
  - It links "How to fix repeated tool calls", which I did not read.
- https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-dynamic-tool-loading
  - Append, never insert, to keep the cache.
  - Pin core tools at the top level.
  - Dynamic loading works only on `kimi-k3.1-pro` and `kimi-k3`. On `kimi-k2.6` it fails with a tokenization error.
  - A `system` message with `tools` plus `content` returns 400.
- https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-kimi-api-to-complete-tool-calls
  - Every `tool_call` needs a `role=tool` message with the correct `tool_call_id`, or the request errors.
  - Independent calls tend to be returned in parallel.
